The same way you'd get into anything. Study & Practice.

Voice Acting is Acting. Plain & simple. Much like music, you've heard a great many performances but hearing tons of music won't make you an incredible musician just like watching many shows won't make you a great actor.

It's not for everyone & isn't an overnight endeavor. Here is what I would personally suggest for anyone wishing to break in :

  • A decent Microphone.
  • Software to playback & edit your recordings.
  • & Patience.

Picking up an instrument you've never played before & trying to play something you just heard may be next to impossible - but you've been speaking your whole life (or most of it) & with the right ear - can mimic an accent, style, or intensity to alter the delivery of common phrases with next to no practice.

I'm not suggesting practicing impressions but, to make a long description short, to experiment with what you're capable of to gauge your range. To some it may come naturally but may require more effort with others.

Listen to yourself, Ask for critique from others & if you feel comfortable enough try to create a Demo
